convoLines.text: "Can we talk?" Clarence sits down near you. "Just... talk. Like people used to."
"Lockpick — It sits up. It hunts at night — give the dark a wide berth."
They glance toward the fire, toward the others — checking who's listening.
"Nope. No." Clarence shakes their head too fast. "I don't know where you're getting this."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
You show them Elderberry — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"Now — Did you leave someone behind? ...Sorry. You don't have to answer that."
Just: "Yeah." A long quiet. "Me too."
"...What's that supposed to mean?" Their voice goes careful.
"Can I be honest? Still on who you left behind."
"Moving! But — good talk! More later!"
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Are you angry? At whoever did this. At the sky. At anything."
"Good. Anger's fuel. Just — point it somewhere useful."
"He lowers the crown. That's Rut King telling you it's about to move. Dawn and dusk, that's when it's out."
"This one — Tucumã. Leaf, stem, smell. You won't forget it now."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
Something crosses their face — quick, then gone. The practiced expression clicks back into place.
"I'm not from Denver. I'm from Sydney, Australia. I wasn't protecting myself. I was protecting someone else."
"Still on whether you're angry."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
They fill the quiet. "Anyway — where was I?"
"Well. My social battery is officially dead."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"You said yes — you left someone behind. I never asked who. I won't. But I'm still here, asking nothing, if that helps."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
They go very still. Not relaxed-still. Held-still.
*They've deflected you before. The evidence needs to be heavier this time — one more thread before you speak.*
"Fine." Sharp. "You want to hear it? I dug it up. I was starving and your hole was right there. Happy now?"
"Still on that personal stuff."
You show them Yarrow — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"About that question — What do you make of all this? Really. Anyway, that's me."
"Well. Bleak. Probably true. I keep looking for the part where it's not."
"Saw things with too many joints. Give them room. That's the whole lesson."
"Still on what you make of all this."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"Walk my trap line with me? Extra hands, extra eyes."
It's quiet at the trap line. Charlotte doesn't say much. Sometimes that's the whole point.
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "I dreamed Scott was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."
"I keep turning over the last thing Scott said to me. I can't tell if I'm remembering it right, and that's somehow the worst part."
"We bury, we grieve, we keep going. There's no step four."
You show them Elderberry — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"This was good." They mean it.
"My wound needs a second pair of hands. Could you clean it out for me? Please."
"It's getting worse, not better. If it festers I'm no good to anyone — can't haul, can't hunt, can't watch. Just clean it out and wrap it tight."
Move next to them, on the same side of the Haven door, to help.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Huh. Let me think about that." "You feel that? The air before a storm. That's the village right now."
"I eat fast and leave early. Not hiding. Just — scheduling."
"It'll break at a moot or it'll break at midnight. I'm betting moot."
"Still on what's been happening."
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"You called this the end of the world. We're still here, though. That's either something, or it's us."
"Help me haul something back? Too much for one."
It's quiet at the cache spot. Charlotte doesn't say much. Sometimes that's the whole point.
"a cellar full of jars — I'll show you on the map sometime. It's real."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on that personal stuff."
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
"Yeah? What's up?"
"Pantry's thin and getting thinner. Will you forage with me tomorrow? Two pairs of eyes, twice the ground."
"I did the count twice. The count doesn't change. I know the old burn east of camp — come with me and we'll fill packs before dark."
There is no playable joint foraging outing yet. Giving food does not perform the promised outing.
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"No, yeah, of course. Forget I asked." They won't forget. They'll just stop asking.
"Right. Go on, then."
"Forget I asked. I'll figure it out."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
Why are you being so nice lately? What's the angle? There's always an angle.
"Take your time."
"an old trapline — I'll show you on the map sometime. It's real."
"Another day like today and we're choosing who eats. Meet me at the piquiarana patch past the treeline and we'll fill packs before dark."
There is no playable joint foraging outing yet. Giving food does not perform the promised outing.
"We were just talking. Nothing important."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"You said you were furious. Most days. Still carrying it?"
"Walk with me? I want another pair of eyes on something."
You walk to the tree line with Charlotte. Nothing much there — but they talk the whole way, and you learn the shape of them a little better.
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Still on that personal stuff. That's still where we are."
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
"Sure — what's on your mind?"
"I did the count twice. The count doesn't change. Meet me at the old burn east of camp and we'll fill packs before dark."
"I just said — did you miss it?"
"I just told you — what else is on your mind?"
"We've covered this one. Ask me something else."
"Well. My social battery is officially dead."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to that favor."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"About the pantry run — the need hasn't gone anywhere. I'm still asking."
"Another day like today and we're choosing who eats. I know where the jujube grows thick — come with me and we'll fill packs before dark."
As I said — There is no playable joint foraging outing yet. Giving food does not perform the promised outing.
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
"Saw things with too many joints. Give them room. That's the whole lesson."
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "They took you — Wheel of Teeth, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
"That's... pretty much all of it, honestly."
"Come see what I found. You won't believe it."
You walk to the hollow with Charlotte. Nothing much there — but they talk the whole way, and you learn the shape of them a little better.
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Still on what's been happening."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Sure. I'll be around."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"It's been a while. Glad we circled back to what's been happening."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"Are you going to stay? With us. For real."
Something eases in their shoulders. "Good. We're better with you here. I mean that."
"Watch for this: The hissing stops. Ducks in a row, every time. It hunts by day — watch the open ground."
"Oh! Still on whether you're staying."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
"Wheel of Teeth. They just... took you. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
You show them Elderberry — where it grows, how to tell it apart. Their eyes widen. "I never knew that."
"I count portions out loud before eating. It passes the time. The time passes anyway."
"Same as always: we endure."
"Okay I really have to move now or I'll explode — talk soon!"
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"This was good." They mean it.
